title: Kamar al-Zaman and the Jeweller's Defense

keywords: kamar al-zaman and the jeweller's wife
full_text:
Kamar al-Zaman, a handsome young gem merchant of Baghdad, was celebrated for his impeccable honesty in evaluating precious stones. His workshop stood adjacent to that of an elderly master jeweler named Ubayd.

During Ubayd’s absence on a purchasing journey to the mines of Golconda, an unscrupulous courtier attempted to extort a valuable diamond necklace from Ubayd’s wife through forged letters and legal intimidation.

Kamar al-Zaman intervened with fearless courage: he examined the forged letters, proved before the city magistrate that the seal was counterfeit, and used his own funds to pay the municipal taxes, guarding his neighbor’s home and honor with the protective care of a brother.

When master Ubayd returned from India and discovered how the young merchant had shielded his household from ruin, he wept with profound gratitude.

Ubayd adopted Kamar al-Zaman as his full commercial partner, bequeathed him his famous jewelry guild, and celebrated his union with his virtuous niece, proving that neighborly loyalty and unselfish courage build lasting prosperity.
moral: Honorable restraint and defending the vulnerable preserve household peace and earn civic respect.
